statement: If a point be taken outside a circle and from the point there fall on the circle two straight lines, if one of them cut the circle, and the other fall on it, and if further the rectangle contained by the whole of the straight line which cuts the circle and the straight line intercepted on it outside between the point and the convex circumference be equal to the square on the straight line which falls on the circle, the straight line which falls on it will touch the circle.
heath_proof: For let a point D be taken outside the circle ABC; from D let the two straight lines DCA, DB fall on the circle ACB; let DCA cut the circle and DB fall on it; and let the rectangle AD, DC be equal to the square on DB. I say that DB touches the circle ABC. For let DE be drawn touching ABC; let the centre of the circle ABC be taken, and let it be F; let FE, FB, FD be joined. Thus the angle FED is right. [III. 18] Now, since DE touches the circle ABC, and DCA cuts it, the rectangle AD, DC is equal to the square on DE. [III. 36] But the rectangle AD, DC was also equal to the square on DB; therefore the square on DE is equal to the square on DB; therefore DE is equal to DB. And FE is equal to FB; therefore the two sides DE, EF are equal to the two sides DB, BF; and FD is the common base of the triangles; therefore the angle DEF is equal to the angle DBF. [I. 8] But the angle DEF is right; therefore the angle DBF is also right. And FB produced is a diameter; and the straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter of a circle, from its extremity, touches the circle; [III. 16] therefore DB touches the circle. Similarly this can be proved to be the case even if the centre be on AC.

**Statement:** If a point be taken outside a circle and from the point there fall on the circle two straight lines, if one of them cut the circle, and the other fall on it, and if further the rectangle contained by the whole of the straight line which cuts the circle and the straight line intercepted on it outside between the point and the convex circumference be equal to the square on the straight line which falls on the circle, the straight line which falls on it will touch the circle.

**Step 1.** Let D be a point taken outside the circle ABC, and from D let the two straight lines DCA and DB fall on the circle; let DCA cut the circle (meeting the circumference at C and at A), and let DB fall on the circle at B; and let the rectangle contained by AD, DC be equal to the square on DB. I say that DB touches the circle ABC.

**Step 2.** From the point D draw the straight line DE touching the circle ABC [3.17]; let F be the centre of the circle ABC [3.1]; and join FE, FB, FD [P1].

**Step 3.** Since DE touches the circle ABC and FE is joined from the centre F to the point of contact E, FE is perpendicular to DE; therefore the angle FED is right [3.18].

**Step 4.** Since DE touches the circle ABC and DCA cuts it, the rectangle contained by AD, DC is equal to the square on DE [3.36].

**Step 5.** But the rectangle contained by AD, DC is also equal to the square on DB, by hypothesis. Therefore the square on DE is equal to the square on DB [CN1]; hence the straight line DE is equal to the straight line DB.

**Step 6.** Moreover FE is equal to FB, since both are drawn from the centre F to the circumference of the circle [D1.15].

**Step 7.** Therefore, in the two triangles DEF, DBF, the two sides DE, EF are equal to the two sides DB, BF respectively (Steps 5 and 6), and the base FD is common to both. Therefore the angle DEF is equal to the angle DBF [1.8].

**Step 8.** But the angle DEF is right (Step 3); therefore the angle DBF is also right.

**Step 9.** Produce BF beyond F to meet the circumference at G [P2]. Then BG, being drawn through the centre F and terminated in both directions by the circumference, is a diameter of the circle ABC [D1.17]. Hence DB is a straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter BG from its extremity B (Step 8).

**Step 10.** But the straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter of a circle from its extremity touches the circle [3.16, Porism]. Therefore DB touches the circle ABC.

Therefore, if a point be taken outside a circle and from the point there fall on the circle two straight lines, if one of them cut the circle and the other fall on it, and if further the rectangle contained by the whole of the straight line which cuts the circle and the straight line intercepted on it outside between the point and the convex circumference be equal to the square on the straight line which falls on the circle, the straight line which falls on it will touch the circle. Q.E.D.
